scientific_question: Can the existing autonomous-assurance route, without any new parameter or empirical retuning, synthetically convert a decline in effective pollinator service into maintained or increased reproduction for some lineages?

model_base.factor_context: full retained v11-style configuration except the matched assurance-route ablation

matched_ablation.assurance_on: use frozen lineage assurance_ceiling and assurance_responsiveness values
matched_ablation.assurance_off: set assurance_ceiling=0 and assurance_responsiveness=0 for every lineage; leave opportunity, local support, partner effectiveness, dependency, trait position and all random streams unchanged

directional_state_definitions.assurance_sign_rescue: service_decline AND assurance_on reproduction_delta >= -epsilon AND assurance_off reproduction_delta < -epsilon
directional_state_definitions.assurance_magnitude_rescue: service_decline AND assurance_on reproduction_delta > assurance_off reproduction_delta + epsilon

primary_decision_rule: If assurance_sign_rescue > 0, conclude that the already-existing assurance route is synthetically sufficient to create at least one buffering state under the frozen model.
If assurance_sign_rescue = 0 but assurance_magnitude_rescue > 0, conclude that assurance changes the magnitude of propagation but has not demonstrated sign-level buffering under this design.
If both are zero, conclude that the existing assurance route does not generate buffering under the frozen design.
secondary_outputs: buffered lineage contrasts with assurance ON
buffered lineage contrasts with assurance OFF
mean service and reproductive deltas under matched ON/OFF runs
forbidden_interpretations: do not call synthetic buffering empirical validation of Hawaiʻi or any other island system
do not infer autonomous assurance is the universal island buffer
do not use the result to admit the Hawaiʻi assurance candidate under the empirical admission interface
do not tune assurance ceilings or responsiveness after this run to increase buffering counts
do not add a generic buffer parameter if assurance fails
next_gate_after_run: Freeze the exact result. If synthetic sign rescue exists, assurance gains synthetic sufficiency only; empirical admission remains governed separately by the frozen buffer-mechanism admission interface. If it does not, retain the failure and move to other source-identified candidates without retuning assurance.
claim_boundary: This is a synthetic mechanism-capability ablation. It tests whether an existing route can generate a qualitative buffering state, not whether that route caused any observed island pattern.
